items.title: 8.1.5 Advanced Information Retrieval Techniques (search engines, keywords, Boolean operators, advanced search features)

source_refs.note: Topic 8.1.5 with the class activity and Did You Know (PDF 197-198, printed 194-195). One example prints 'a student in wants'. MCQ 2 is answered (c); the key gives (a). Short question 5 is answered. Recorded.

items: Effective search queries: be specific; 'traditional Pakistani recipes' gives better results than 'recipes'.
Effective keywords: use the most important words of the topic; 'organic farming' rather than just 'farming'.
Boolean operators: AND includes both terms (agriculture AND irrigation), OR includes either (crops OR vegetables), NOT excludes a term (farming NOT pesticides).
Advanced search features: filter by date, location and more; for the latest news on Pakistan's education policy, limit results to the past year.

blocks.alt: Top: three pairs of overlapping circles. For agriculture AND irrigation only the overlap is shaded; for crops OR vegetables both circles are shaded; for farming NOT pesticides only the part of farming outside pesticides is shaded. Bottom left: five types of online research. Bottom right: five components of digital literacy.
blocks.caption: Boolean searches, types of online research and digital literacy (original diagram after topic 8.1).
blocks.long_description: AND returns only pages containing both words, the overlap of the two circles, so it narrows a search; OR returns pages with either word, the whole of both circles, so it widens a search; NOT returns pages with the first word but not the second, cutting the overlap away. Online research may be general, academic, market, fact-checking or health research. Digital literacy combines using technology, searching, evaluating sources, creating content and staying safe and private.

blocks.text: The book notes that more than half of the world's population uses the internet, so researching well online is a powerful skill (Did You Know).

blocks.prompt: Which Boolean operator excludes a term (MCQ 2)? Why use specific keywords (short question 5)?
blocks.explanation: (c) NOT. Specific keywords tell the search engine exactly what you want, so the results are relevant and you spend less time sorting through unrelated pages.

blocks.prompt: Class activity: research a topic with specific keywords, find three sources, judge their reliability and summarize with links. What makes a good summary?
blocks.explanation: The main facts in your own words, a note on why each source is reliable (or not), and the link to each source.

items: Search better: specific queries and keywords, Boolean AND/OR/NOT, advanced filters.
